name: Kathy Osterman Beach
description: A generous crescent of pale sand, neighborhood picnics, and a horizon that seems to go on forever.
fact: Locals also call this Hollywood Beach, after the nearby avenue.
practical: Check the Park District’s daily swimming status and posted lifeguard hours.
story: Begin where the lakefront feels like a neighborhood. Edgewater’s apartment buildings stand behind the park, while the horizon stays wide and open. It is a gentle introduction to a route that will eventually pass harbors, downtown towers, grand museums, and the parks of the South Side.

You may hear two names for the same place. Hollywood Beach takes its familiar name from the nearby avenue; Kathy Osterman Beach honors a Chicago public servant. Both belong to the life of this part of the city.

For a small first outing, connect Osterman with Foster Beach. For a full day, continue south toward Montrose. There is no requirement to reach the other end: the point of a lakefront journey is having room to stop.

The main trail lies inland of the beach. Follow the signed connections, leave room for people crossing toward the sand, and check the Park District’s current swimming information before entering the water.

name: Montrose Point Bird Sanctuary
description: Step into the Magic Hedge. The skyline recedes, and the smallest movement in the leaves becomes the main event.
fact: More than 300 bird species have been recorded in the sanctuary and adjacent dunes.
practical: Explore on foot, stay on marked paths, and observe birds at a distance.
story: The best way to visit the Point is to slow down. In the brush, a small movement can turn into a warbler; over the water, a distant shape can become something entirely different through binoculars. The city is still close, but it stops demanding your attention.

The sanctuary and adjacent dunes have recorded more than 300 bird species. The 150-yard stretch of shrubs and trees known as the Magic Hedge is particularly associated with spring and fall migration. It offers shelter along a much larger route followed by birds.

Leave the through trail for a quiet walk. Stay on marked paths, avoid crowding wildlife, and let binoculars bring you closer. You do not need a long species list to enjoy a few minutes of looking carefully.
